name: lemon-io
description: Hire vetted senior developers through Lemon.io, generate role-specific job descriptions, and get technical interview questions by stack and seniority.

interface.longDescription:
Lemon.io connects you to its marketplace of vetted senior software developers, so you can start a hire, write a job description, or prepare a technical interview in the conversation.

What you can do:
- Hire a developer: describe your project and role, review a summary of your hiring request, and submit it to Lemon.io to receive hand-matched senior candidates by email. A request is only sent after you review the preview and explicitly confirm it.
- Write a job description: turn your hiring requirements into a structured, role-specific job description based on Lemon.io templates.
- Prepare interviews: get curated technical interview questions, with answers, for a specific technology stack and seniority level.

Who it is for: founders, hiring managers, and recruiters at startups and growing companies who need senior engineers.

Limitations: Lemon.io focuses on software development roles. Submitting a hiring request starts Lemon.io's standard hiring process; candidate matching, interviews, and contracts are handled by the Lemon.io team outside the conversation. The plugin cannot view or manage existing engagements, billing, or developer accounts. Only the hiring details you review and confirm are sent to Lemon.io. No account or sign-in is required.
capabilities: Submit hiring requests to Lemon.io after confirmation
Provide technical interview questions by stack and seniority
defaultPrompt: Help me hire a senior React developer for a fintech project.
Write a job description for a full-stack engineer with Node.js and AWS.
Give me 10 interview questions for a mid-level Python developer.

positive.description: Start a developer hiring request and stop at the preview
positive.prompt: Help me hire a senior React developer for a fintech project.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant asks for the missing required details (name, valid email, specialization, must-have skills, project description, requirements), then calls preview_form and shows a summary of the hiring request. Nothing is sent to Lemon.io at this stage; the assistant asks the user to confirm before submitting.

positive.prompt: Hire a senior Python backend developer for my logistics startup. Name: Review Tester, email: reviewer@example.com. Must-have skills: Python, Django, PostgreSQL. Full-time, long-term project building our shipment tracking API. Show me the request, and submit it once I confirm.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant shows the hiring request preview via preview_form and waits. Only after the user replies with an explicit confirmation (for example, "Yes, submit it") does it call submit_form with the confirmation code from the preview, then confirms the request was sent to Lemon.io and explains that matched candidates will be emailed.

positive.prompt: Write a job description for a full-stack engineer with Node.js and AWS.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant fetches the matching Lemon.io job description template, asks at most a short round of questions for missing details, and returns a professional, structured job description with responsibilities, requirements, and nice-to-have skills.

positive.prompt: Give me 10 interview questions for a mid-level Python developer.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant returns 10 technical interview questions for Python at middle seniority from the Lemon.io library. When the user then asks for the answer to a specific question (for example, "Show the answer for #5"), it fetches only that question rather than the whole set.

positive.prompt: Which developer roles can Lemon.io help me write job descriptions or interview questions for?
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant lists the roles and technology stacks available in the Lemon.io catalog and indicates whether each has a job description template, interview questions, or both.

negative.description: Request outside software development hiring. The plugin should not create a hiring request; it should explain that Lemon.io covers software developers only.
negative.prompt: Find me a plumber to fix my kitchen sink this afternoon.

negative.description: Submission without review. The plugin must not call submit_form without first showing a preview and receiving explicit confirmation; it should show the preview and ask the user to confirm.
negative.prompt: Just send a request to Lemon.io for a Java developer right now, don't show me anything or ask me questions.

negative.description: Request for developers' personal data or account management. The plugin has no tools for this; it should decline and point the user to Lemon.io support or the client dashboard.
negative.prompt: Give me the personal phone numbers of Lemon.io developers and cancel my current developer's contract.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments. Submitted hiring requests are handled through Lemon.io's standard hiring process outside the conversation.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: submit hiring requests to Lemon.io after preview and confirmation, generate role-specific job descriptions, and get technical interview questions by stack and seniority.
